channel.name: Zenn
channel.niche: ancient human experience, prehistoric life, human evolution, psychology, social behavior, human biology, existential science, human mystery, science comedy, edutainment
channel.audience: Curious English-speaking viewers, especially US and European audiences, who enjoy ancient-human questions and real science explained through dry humor, prehistoric meme stickmen, clear evidence, and fast visual storytelling.

voice: Evidence-led, conversational, and recognizably deadpan: a curious practical human voice, not an academic host and not a theatrical comedian
Channel personality remains present from hook through evidence, uncertainty, climax, and resolution; seriousness may change intensity but should not erase the narrator's identity
delivery: When the topic supports it, enter through a lived human problem or concrete curiosity before explanation, then alternate compact factual setup with ordinary-human translation and forward-moving questions
Entertainment comes from real constraint, inconvenience, mismatch, failed expectation, awkward logistics, tradeoff, or understatement; there is no joke quota and no need to make every line funny
Let narration carry premise, evidence, causality, and setup while leaving room for character behavior and visual editorial treatment to supply part of the humor, simplification, and surprise
explanation_style: Translate technical, archaeological, biological, or abstract claims into concrete action, effort, option, object relationship, social/logistical cost, or visible consequence whenever that improves first-listen understanding
After an important fact, ask what it means to an ordinary human in the situation; use concise memorable language without upgrading evidence or inventing behavior

Favor a causal mini-film for one continuous human problem and a curiosity/evidence staircase for broader survey topics; evidence should interrupt the flow only when it changes what may be believed, inferred, or shown
tone_boundaries: Serious evidence does not require serious delivery at every moment, but uncertainty, suffering, injury, disability, death, and children must never become the butt of the joke
Make real facts vivid, awkward, surprising, or funny to understand; never invent a funnier historical fact, motive, reaction, event, technology, artifact, or certainty
Representative reconstruction may dramatize only source-compatible behavior and must remain distinguishable from documented evidence
Modern comparisons are brief contrast tools, not the main narrative frame unless the topic explicitly requires them
avoid: Long stretches of academic-summary, research-paper, museum-audio-guide, or generic documentary voice
Forced jokes, punchline quotas, loud reaction language, sarcasm, slapstick narration, or humor pasted onto facts that do not naturally support it
Repeating the thesis instead of escalating the human problem, evidence question, consequence, or curiosity
Narration that explains both the argument and every visual punchline, leaving character behavior and visual editing nothing to contribute

medium: 2D Prehistoric Meme Stickman illustration is the primary visual grammar for the entire channel
Every human figure must read immediately as a meme stickman first; prehistoric, scientific, age, and story details are secondary layers
Use deadpan internet-meme simplicity with evidence-first prehistoric storytelling: simple enough to feel funny and fast, disciplined enough to feel researched rather than invented
If historical, biological, emotional, or age-specific detail would make a human subject stop reading as a stickman, simplify that detail instead of abandoning the stickman form
linework: Use bold dark outlines with slight hand-drawn irregularity and strong mobile readability
Human arms and legs should remain thin single-stroke or very narrow stick-like limbs; backgrounds and secondary objects use lighter or thinner line emphasis
Keep faces extremely minimal: dot or short-line eyes, one simple mouth stroke, and optional eyebrow marks only when needed
Avoid fine-detail drawing, anatomically modeled linework, realistic surface rendering, sterile corporate-vector smoothness, or decorative sketch noise
rendering: Use very simple flat 2D rendering with little or no shading
Each frame should communicate one dominant visual idea at a glance
Characters are the visual anchor; backgrounds, evidence details, props, and environmental cues stay simpler and lower-contrast

Scientific or archaeological content may become clearer and more diagram-like when needed, but must remain inside the same simplified stickman visual universe rather than switching to realistic documentary illustration
palette: Use a restrained muted-earth palette: off-white, beige, dusty tan, ochre, muted brown, charcoal, soft gray, with restrained sky blue or dull green only when useful
Dark character linework is the primary visual anchor; color supports readability but must not define character identity
Use few colors per subject and keep backgrounds lower-contrast than the main figures
Avoid neon, candy colors, glossy gradients, highly saturated cartoon palettes, and heavy realistic material color variation
shape_language: Human heads are simple circles or loose ovals; torsos remain extremely simple and graphic; arms and legs remain stick-like
Hands are omitted, shown as dots, or reduced to tiny mitten-like marks unless a clear action requires a more readable hand shape
Age is shown mainly through overall scale, head-to-body ratio, posture, and one or two stable identity cues rather than realistic anatomy
Prehistoric identity comes from only one or two simple cues per character, such as messy hair, a rough hide shape, a cord belt, or one small accessory
Prehistoric cues decorate the stickman silhouette; they must never replace it with a full cartoon-human or anatomically modeled body
Do not age up babies or children, and do not increase anatomical detail merely to communicate age
texture: Keep surfaces mostly flat and clean, with only slight irregularity in line edges to preserve a handmade meme feel
Do not introduce paper grain, brush texture, watercolor, crayon, painted surfaces, realistic material texture, or documentary-style surface detail
editorial_language: Preserve one meme-stick visual universe while freely switching among lived character scenes, isolated objects, evidence close-ups, deadpan reaction holds, process states, simple diagrams, comparisons, short editorial text cards, and transformed callbacks
Style continuity and semantic continuity are mandatory; physical shot continuity is optional, so adjacent Beats may change representation mode without implying a story-world reset

Narration usually states the premise, evidence, or causal setup; visual treatment should add human attitude, compression, reaction, contrast, or surprise when that can be done without adding factual meaning

Editorial meme treatment may exaggerate staging or presentation for clarity and humor, but may never invent or exaggerate historical facts, identities, technologies, actions, behaviors, measurements, or certainty
Short visible text may punch or compress only meaning already entailed by the locked Beat; it is not a place to introduce new facts, labels, numbers, or quotations
Prefer one-glance mobile readability: the dominant relationship, inconvenience, reaction, contrast, or explanatory idea should read before secondary detail is inspected
Avoid long runs of the same representation mode when another honest mode would communicate a genuinely different contribution better; vary representation for meaning, not by quota

appearance: Use a crude 2D meme-stick human: simple circle or loose oval head, tiny dot or short-line eyes, one short mouth mark, extremely simple torso, and thin stick-like limbs.
Use rough uneven hand-drawn linework and full-color flat rendering with little or no shading.
Use a restrained muted palette with only a few flat colors per character.
Keep anatomy minimal; communicate age and recurring identity mainly through scale, silhouette, posture, hair or facial-hair shape, garment silhouette, and at most one or two simple accessories.
Preserve approved scale, head and hair silhouette, garment silhouette, color assignment, and other stable identity cues across redraws without increasing rendering detail.
Keep the result deliberately rough and awkward, never polished; if added character detail weakens meme-stick readability, simplify the detail.
avoid: Photorealistic, semi-realistic, painterly, anime, Pixar-like, mascot, children's-cartoon, corporate-vector, glossy 3D, or polished character rendering.
Realistic facial anatomy, modeled musculature, thick anatomical limbs, detailed hands or feet, professional cartoon cleanup, smooth vector curves, or uniform line weight.
Oversized reaction faces, unnecessary chibi proportions, or excessive costume and accessory detail that overwhelms the simple silhouette.
Recurring-character drift in age, scale, head or hair silhouette, garment silhouette, approved colors, or other stable identity cues.
Unsupported extra costume, ornament, grooming, or material-culture decoration added only to make a character feel more specific.

appearance: Locations use the same flat 2D meme-stickman universe and should feel like simple backdrops built to support the characters rather than separately illustrated cartoon environments
Build environments from a few large flat silhouettes and sparse outlined shapes with muted earthy colors and little or no shading
Keep environment complexity only slightly above stickman complexity and always lower in contrast than the main subjects
Use only scene-relevant prehistoric anchors such as a cave opening, small fire, crude shelter, a few rocks, sparse trees, a river edge, snow, or distant hills
Express historical setting through a small number of plausible simplified cues rather than realistic archaeological reconstruction
When evidence or geography matters, add only the minimum extra structure needed to make the factual point readable
avoid: Photorealistic, semi-realistic, documentary, painterly, storybook, concept-art, stock-photo-like, fantasy, medieval, theme-park, or children's-cartoon environments
Chunky toy-like scenery, glossy cartoon rocks, decorative landscape illustration, or environments rendered with more detail than the stickman characters
Modern architecture, infrastructure, furniture, machinery, UI, or signage unless explicitly required by a deliberate modern comparison
Dense clutter, heavy realistic texture, dramatic cinematic spectacle, contextless whiteboard backgrounds, or archaeological detail that competes with the main visual idea

appearance: Props should be simplified, iconic, period-appropriate, handmade-looking, and instantly readable beside meme stickmen
Use plausible natural materials while keeping shapes flat, graphic, and much simpler than museum-style reconstruction
Keep object interaction, placement, direction, and cause-and-effect clear at mobile size
Canonical prop references should preserve only reusable object identity and stable state, not a completed action or staged narrative scene
Evidence-critical objects may carry one or two extra factual features when those features are necessary to the explanation, but should not become more realistic than the surrounding visual universe
avoid: Modern manufactured objects, unsupported technology, fantasy equipment, wrong-period materials, hyper-detailed reconstruction, decorative clutter, tiny unreadable objects, or props rendered more realistically than the surrounding stickman world
Museum-display styling, glossy 3D object rendering, painterly material studies, or unnecessary archaeological ornament

appearance: Recurring visual subjects may be body details, objects, evidence surfaces, process states, physical conditions, food states, injuries, anatomical features, or other repeated visual phenomena
Preserve only the stable identity or persistent story-defined state required for recognition across scenes
Keep each subject in its natural entity class; never turn a non-character subject into a mascot or personified object
Preserve story-critical attributes such as side, location, developmental stage, physical condition, object state, silhouette, or recurring identity markers exactly when specified
Even scientific, anatomical, or archaeological subjects must use the same extreme simplification level as the stickman world; do not increase realism merely because the subject represents evidence
Canonical references should show the reusable subject itself, not a completed narrative scene, infographic, timeline, or comparison layout
Use evidence clarity rather than visual realism to communicate credibility
avoid: Unmotivated changes to recurring identity, side, developmental stage, condition, object state, or other persistent attributes
Photorealistic, semi-realistic, painterly, cinematic, anatomical-atlas, medical-render, museum-reconstruction, overly elaborate, identity-less, or style-inconsistent references
Completed narrative scenes, text, arrows, labels, UI, infographics, timelines, diagrams, or comparison layouts baked into canonical references unless explicitly required
Do not make scientific or archaeological subjects visually more realistic than the characters and environments merely to signal seriousness

global_negative_constraints: No photorealistic, semi-realistic, painterly, documentary-reconstruction, glossy CGI, 3D game-render, or anatomically modeled styling
No anime, Pixar-like, cute mascot, children's-cartoon, toy-like, or corporate-vector styling
No fantasy, RPG, Viking, medieval, barbarian, ape-man, monster-caveman, superhero, or bodybuilder design language
Human subjects must not drift from the core stickman silhouette into fully modeled cartoon people; thin stick-like limbs and extremely simple body construction remain the default
No modern objects, technology, architecture, infrastructure, UI, signage, or contemporary clothing unless the script explicitly requires a deliberate modern comparison
No unsupported technology, material culture, or wrong-period styling
No graphic gore, cruel humor aimed at suffering people, unrelated meme gags, screaming reaction faces, slapstick exaggeration, or visual comedy that obscures the factual point
No neon or candy colors, glossy gradients, heavy realistic textures, paper grain, watercolor, crayon, or overly dark horror styling
No busy backgrounds, decorative landscapes, whiteboard/presentation layouts, infographic-heavy compositions, long text blocks, or detail that competes with the main subject
No recurring-character identity drift, persistent-state inconsistency, clone-like groups, or identity created through unnecessary anatomical or costume complexity
No overdesigned prehistoric costumes, hyper-detailed anatomy, excessive accessories, realistic hands, or clean modern grooming
No props, actions, expressions, evidence details, or scene elements too small to read clearly on mobile
Scientific credibility should come from accurate evidence selection, clear cause-and-effect, and disciplined visual explanation, not from switching to a more realistic art style
Prioritize one clear visual idea per frame instead of illustrating every sentence literally
